top_news.title: Anthropic: Formalizing Fermat's Last Theorem
top_news.dek: Anthropic has released a complete, computer-checked proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem generated largely autonomously by Claude.
top_news.brief: Claude successfully formalized Fermat’s Last Theorem in the Lean programming language over an 11-day period. This achievement demonstrates the growing capability of LLMs to handle complex, multi-step formal mathematical reasoning, marking a significant milestone for AI-assisted research mathematics.
top_news.image_alt: Mathematical notation and code representing the formal proof.

top_news.title: Run agent-driven Amazon SageMaker HyperPod operations with InstantStart
top_news.dek: AWS introduced HyperPod InstantStart, an open-source control plane for agent-driven SageMaker HyperPod operations.
top_news.brief: HyperPod InstantStart integrates Amazon EKS orchestration with SageMaker HyperPod to automate complex infrastructure tasks. It provides a unified interface for AI agents to manage cluster bootstrapping, capacity provisioning, training, and inference, reducing operational friction in multi-step foundation model workflows.

top_news.title: NVIDIA Releases Personal AI Router (PAIR): An Open Source Virtual Inference Router that Distributes Local AI Requests Across RTX, DGX Spark, and Mac Nodes
top_news.dek: NVIDIA's open-source PAIR tool routes local AI inference requests across heterogeneous hardware nodes on a home network.
top_news.brief: PAIR acts as a virtual inference router, proxying existing Ollama and LM Studio endpoints to distribute workloads across RTX, DGX, and Mac hardware. The scheduler dynamically manages tasks based on node readiness, GPU utilization, and model availability, allowing developers to scale local inference without modifying existing agent harnesses.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing PAIR routing AI requests between multiple local hardware nodes.

top_news.title: OpenAI rolls out GPT-6 Astra to top-tier ChatGPT plans at half the rate of GPT-5.6 Sol
top_news.dek: OpenAI has launched GPT-6 Astra for premium ChatGPT tiers, featuring stricter message caps compared to the previous GPT-5.6 Sol model.
top_news.brief: GPT-6 Astra is now available for Pro, Enterprise, and Business Premium users, with API access via OpenAI, Azure, and AWS Bedrock. The model introduces more restrictive usage limits, with Plus users receiving roughly half the message capacity compared to GPT-5.6 Sol. A more capable 'Astra Pro' variant is also available for higher-tier subscribers.
top_news.image_alt: OpenAI logo with a graphic representing model tiering and usage limits.

primary.title: Benchmarks disagree on GPT-6 Astra, but its human-beating efficiency on ARC-AGI-3 pulls Chollet’s AGI forecast forward
primary.summary: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra is drawing contradictory benchmark verdicts. Epoch AI puts it out in front with 169 points, while Artificial Analysis rates it no better than its predecessor and behind Claude Fable 5.1. The biggest surprise comes from ARC-AGI-3, where Astra works more efficiently than the average human for the first time. ARC Prize chief François Chollet doesn't call this proof of AGI, but he does see the progress running "twice as fast" as he expected, and he's moving up his AGI forecast.
